title: Study for the painting “Intake”
lede: Bridget Riley’s black poster-colour study of 1964: wavy black and white bands that tighten into one corner.
summary: Black and white curved bands that narrow and bunch toward the top right corner. Bridget Riley, study for Intake, 1964.

source.label: V&A: Study for the painting “Intake”, CIRC.237-1965

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected the V&A image of its copy, CIRC.237-1965 (1552 × 1600 px), in a scratchpad. No image is stored.

styles.note: A clear black and white Riley study: stripes that change width and direction by steps, so the flat sheet seems to flow.

context: The V&A catalogues the drawing with the style “Op Art”: pencil and black poster colour on paper, 26.3 × 29.4 cm, acquired by the V&A Circulation Department in 1965. [V&A](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O1036839/).

The V&A’s general Riley text also says she designed the Woolmark logo while at an advertising agency. That claim conflicts with the usual attribution of the logo to [Franco Grignani](ref:grignani-woolmark-logo-1964), and it is not repeated here as fact. [V&A](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O1036839/).
observed: Alternating black and white bands run from the lower left toward the top right corner inside a square.
At the lower left the bands are broad and gently curved; toward the top right they narrow, bend more, and converge.
The bands are flat and hard-edged, painted in solid black with no tone.
A narrow grey mount shows around the square.
interpretation: The study isolates the core op device of the style: a stripe field that changes width by steps until the eye reads movement and depth.
Its hand-painted scale shows that Riley’s effects were planned in small studies before the large paintings.
borrow: Run a stripe field diagonally and let it converge into one corner to create a strong direction.
Change stripe width and curvature together, not separately, so that the field seems to turn in space.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The work is by a living artist, and the V&A image is not openly licensed.
